references.text: Moses' staff is transformed into a snake for the first time as a sign from God
The immediate fulfillment of this verse, where Aaron throws his staff before Pharaoh and it becomes a snake
God commands Moses to take the staff that will be used to perform signs
God speaks about wonders (mofetim) that Moses is to perform before Pharaoh
Signs and wonders (mofet) as confirmation of divine authority
Reference to tanin (sea monster/dragon) as a symbol of chaotic forces
Pharaoh is compared to tanin, the great sea monster
The Pharisees ask Jesus for a sign, paralleling Pharaoh's demand for signs
Stephen speaks about Moses performing wonders and signs in Egypt
Direct narrative connection between prophecy (7:9) and fulfillment (7:15) of the same sign.
Same narrative context: Instruction to Aaron to use the staff for a new sign against Pharaoh.
Theological principle regarding the role of the spokesperson (Moses-Aaron-Pharaoh) concretized in both verses.
Contrastive parallel: The staff used as judgment over Egypt (snake) versus the staff used for provision in the wilderness.
Same narrative structure: Instruction to Aaron to use the staff for a new sign (gnats).
Direct narrative follow-up: Same instruction (staff over water) for the first plague.
